**Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine.** Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.
[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/15d4Yv__KHeHjshVb-6PRTfqVllxih2S3?usp=sharing) [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/laya.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/laya/) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-2ea44f)](https://nandhakishorm.github.io/laya/) [![Hugging Face Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Model-convaiinnovations%2Flaya-blue)](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya) [![Multilingual](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Model-laya--multilingual-blue)](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual) [![Hugging Face Space](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Space-laya--demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/convaiinnovations/laya-demo) [![Dev.to Article](https://img.shields.io/badge/dev.to-Read%20Article-0A0A0A?logo=devdotto&logoColor=white)](https://dev.to/nandakishor_m_6cc0adfde9f/i-built-non-autoregressive-decision-models-a-year-ago-then-a-frontier-lab-called-it-a-18me) [![Buy Me A Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20A%20Coffee-nandakishorm-FFDD00?logo=buy-me-a-coffee&logoColor=black)](https://www.buymeacoffee.com/nandakishorm) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
## Installation ```bash python -m pip install laya ``` With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), run `uv add laya` in a uv project or `uv pip install laya` in a virtual environment. Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras: `laya[serve]` (HTTP server), `laya[mcp]` (MCP server), `laya[langchain]` (LangChain and LangGraph), `laya[llamaindex]` (LlamaIndex selectors), `laya[crewai]` (CrewAI routing), `laya[onnx]` (ONNX Runtime), `laya[fast]` (TileLang GPU fast path), `laya[structured]` (pydantic models in `decide`). Step-by-step setup for each platform, CPU-only or GPU PyTorch builds, and troubleshooting are in [Installation details](#installation-details). For TypeScript / Node.js / browser, see [`laya-ts/`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/tree/main/laya-ts/). npm releases (`npm install laya-ts`) are published from this repository's `laya-ts-v*` release tags. **Long documents.** `laya-multilingual` reads up to 8,192 tokens with `max_len=8192`. Measured accuracy and time by document length, reproducible with [`research/scripts/bench_long_context.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/research/scripts/bench_long_context.py):

## Quickstart One argument puts vegaml's engine under laya's names: a frozen 0.8B reader with a small physics engine on top, so every answer carries a conformal prediction set, an abstain flag, an out-of-distribution flag and a route decided without a threshold you had to guess at. Text, images, speech and 73k-token documents go through the same call. Python 3.10 or newer; details in [vega inside laya](#vega-inside-laya-agentvegamltrue). ```bash python -m pip install -U laya # 0.4.23 or newer: vegaml comes with it ``` ```python import laya agent = laya.Agent(vegaml=True) # the 0.8B universal reader; vegaml="4b" for the larger one state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan." questions = { "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors", "other": "everything else"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?", "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]}, "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"}, } out = agent.predict(state, questions) ans = out["answers"]["department"] print(ans["choice"]) # billing print(ans["probabilities"]) # {"billing": 0.91, "technical": 0.04, "other": 0.05} print(ans["prediction_set"]) # ["billing"]: the options the answer could still be, at alpha 0.1 print(ans["abstain"]) # False: the engine is not refusing this one print(ans["unbound"]) # False: the state looks like something it has seen print(ans["route"]) # "auto"; "review" when the set, abstain or unbound say so print(out["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"]) # probability the answer is yes ``` The output keeps laya's shape (`choice`, `score`, `noul`, `probabilities`, `answer_confidence`) and adds vega's fields. Gate on `route`, not on a confidence number: it comes from the conformal set and the fitted band, which stay right on answers where the top probability does not. **Model switching.** Keep a laya encoder for short English text and let vega take the rest: ```python from laya.vega import Router router = Router(fast=laya.Agent(), vega=agent) out = router.predict(state, questions) print(out["routing"]) # {"model": "fast", "reason": "short English text, no fitted head: the fast encoder is enough"} out = router.predict("मुझसे मार्च में दो बार शुल्क लिया गया, कृपया डुप्लिकेट राशि वापस करें।", questions) print(out["routing"]["model"]) # vega: non-English goes to the reader ``` The rule, in order: an image or audio goes to vega; text longer than the fast model's context goes to vega; non-English or non-Latin text goes to vega; a question with a fitted head goes to vega; everything else goes to the encoder. `model="vega"` or `model="fast"` forces one. **Images, speech, video, long documents.** The questions and the answer shape do not change with the input: ```python # text: up to 73,728 tokens in one pass; usage["truncated"] says if a state hit the limit agent.predict_long(seventy_page_contract, questions) # image: PIL image, path or HxWx3 array, any format Pillow opens; scaled to ~1 megapixel, no file-size cap agent.predict(image="invoice.png", questions=questions) # audio: path or bytes (wav, flac, ogg, mp3; needs soundfile) or a 1-D waveform with sampling_rate=; # any length, resampled to 16 kHz, transcribed in 30 s windows, transcript counts toward the 73,728 tokens agent.predict(audio=wave, questions=questions, sampling_rate=16000) # video: path or bytes, any container ffmpeg opens, any length and resolution (needs the ffmpeg binary); # speech is transcribed and decided as text, a silent clip is decided on 4 sampled frames as one image agent.predict(video="call.mp4", questions=questions) ``` **Fit and calibrate on your own labels.** Seconds, no gradient step, and the route is decided for you. Labels are a CSV with a `state` column and one column per question id; [`examples/data/routing_labels.csv`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/data/routing_labels.csv) is a 60-row example that routes messages to billing, HR, PR, sales or technical and rates their urgency: ```csv state,team,urgency "We were charged twice for the March invoice, please refund the duplicate.",billing,2 "I would like to apply for the open backend engineer role. Where do I send my CV?",hr,0 "A journalist from the Economic Times is asking for a comment on today's outage.",pr,2 ``` The whole loop, from import to the answer, is [`examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py). It holds out 4 rows per team (20), fits on the other 40, and measures the same 20 rows before and after. Condensed: ```python import csv, laya questions = { "team": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this message?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "hr": "jobs, payroll, leave, policy", "pr": "press, media, public statements", "sales": "pricing, demos, quotes, trials", "technical": "bugs, outages, API and product questions"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How soon does this need a reply?", "criteria": ["can wait", "this week", "today"]}, } rows = list(csv.DictReader(open("examples/data/routing_labels.csv"))) held, fit_rows = rows[-20:], rows[:-20] # the script holds out 4 per team; same idea agent = laya.Agent(vegaml=True) print(laya.VegaAgent.min_rows(questions)) # 35: the fewest rows fit() accepts for these questions before = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] # the cold engine report = agent.fit([{"state": r["state"], "gold": {"team": r["team"], "urgency": r["urgency"]}} for r in fit_rows], questions=questions) # or agent.fit("examples/data/routing_labels.csv", questions=questions) print(report["n_fit"], report["n_calibrate"]) # 30 fit the heads, 10 are held out inside fit() to calibrate on print(report["serving"]) # the questions whose head beat the engine on the same rows print(report["calibration"]["band"]) # the review line per question, or None where it could not hold after = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] agent.save_calibration("fit-routing/") # heads + calibration; agent.load_calibration("fit-routing/") later ``` What the script printed on a laptop GPU, every number measured in that run: ``` minimum rows fit() accepts for these questions: 35 (5 per option of the widest question for the heads, plus a quarter held out to calibrate on, never fewer than 10) == before: the cold engine, 20 held-out rows team accuracy 0.600 ECE 0.221 mean confidence 0.629 urgency accuracy 0.400 ECE 0.412 MAE 0.65 levels team set sizes {1: 13, 2: 7} abstain 12 route {'auto': 6, 'review': 14} == fit + calibrate on 40 rows in 9s: 30 fit the heads, 10 held out to calibrate on team head cv 0.767 vs engine 0.633 on the same rows -> SERVED urgency head cv 0.400 vs engine 0.400 on the same rows -> left to the engine team temperature 0.83 conformal q-hat 0.987 ECE on the calibration rows 0.281 -> 0.241 urgency temperature 6.44 conformal q-hat 0.741 ECE on the calibration rows 0.515 -> 0.142 review line per question: {'team': None, 'urgency': None} ['team', 'urgency']: no line holds precision 0.95 with a 95% bound on 10 calibration rows, so the conformal set routes those answers == after: heads + calibration, 20 held-out rows team accuracy 0.900 ECE 0.206 mean confidence 0.749 urgency accuracy 0.400 ECE 0.059 MAE 0.65 levels team set sizes {2: 2, 3: 2, 4: 6, 5: 10} abstain 0 route {'review': 20} == change on held-out rows: team accuracy +0.300, team ECE -0.015, urgency MAE +0.00 == one held-out message: "Why was a late fee added to this month's bill when we paid on the due " (gold: billing) before: {"choice": "billing", "probabilities": {"billing": 0.999995, "hr": 3e-06, "pr": 0.0, "sales": 1e-06, "technical": 1e-06}, "answer_confidence": 0.999995, "prediction_set": ["billing"], "abstain": false, "unbound": false, "readout": "engine", "route": "auto", "route_reason": "conformal singleton, not abstaining, in distribution"} after: {"choice": "billing", "probabilities": {"billing": 0.674496, "hr": 0.186172, "pr": 0.068743, "sales": 0.041369, "technical": 0.029221}, "answer_confidence": 0.674496, "prediction_set": ["billing", "hr", "pr", "sales", "technical"], "abstain": false, "unbound": null, "readout": "ttt", "route": "review", "route_reason": "band could not hold precision 0.95 on 10 calibration rows, so the conformal rule decides: conformal set at alpha 0.1 holds 5 options"} == ablation: fitting rows per team, same 20 held-out rows per team rows team acc team ECE urg. acc urg. MAE route cold 0 0.600 0.221 0.400 0.65 {'auto': 6, 'review': 14} 7 35 0.800 0.111 0.400 0.65 {'auto': 14, 'review': 6} 8 40 0.900 0.206 0.400 0.65 {'review': 20} ``` Read it honestly. The head took routing from 0.600 to 0.900 on rows it never saw, and was refused for urgency because it did not beat the engine on the same rows, so that question stayed exactly where it was. The urgency ECE fell from 0.412 to 0.059 from a temperature alone, with the argmax untouched. Routing is where 10 calibration rows are too few: at alpha 0.1 the conformal quantile on 10 rows is the largest score, so the sets are wide, and no review line can certify 0.95 precision with a 95% bound on fewer than about 50 rows; the output says so in `route_reason` instead of pretending. The floor of 35 rows gets you a served head; a route you can act on wants a few hundred rows, and `report["calibration"]["band"]` tells you when you are there. How this differs from fine-tuning: a fine-tune runs a gradient through the model until it agrees with your labels, which changes every answer the model gives, invalidates any calibration fitted before, and leaves you a new checkpoint to validate. `fit` never touches the reader. It fits a small logistic head per question over the frozen features, a convex problem with one solution, keeps the head only if it beats chance under cross-validation and serves it only if it also beats the zero-shot engine on the same rows, so a fit can lose and say so, as urgency did above. A quarter of the rows is held out inside `fit` and `calibrate` refits three numbers per question on them: a temperature, a conformal threshold so the prediction set covers at 90%, and the review line, placed where precision holds at 0.95 with a 95% Wilson bound to spare. Every other question is untouched by construction, nothing is forgotten, and `agent.thresholds()` prints what decides `route` right now. ### The laya checkpoints, without vegaml Leave the argument out and laya is the ModernBERT family it always was: ~150M to 421M parameters, 33 ms a decision on a T4, 100+ languages through the `Router`. ```python from laya import Router router = Router() # downloads a checkpoint on first use; Router(preload=True) loads all three up front result = router.predict(state, questions) print(result["answers"]["department"]["choice"]) # billing print(result["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"]) # probability the answer is yes print(result["routing"]["model"]) # english ``` The `Router` detects the script and language and sends non-English text to `laya-multilingual`: ```python for text in ["मुझसे मार्च में दो बार शुल्क लिया गया, कृपया डुप्लिकेट राशि वापस करें।", "La aplicación se cierra cada vez que abro la configuración."]: r = router.predict(text, {"department": questions["department"]}) print(r["routing"]["model"], r["answers"]["department"]["choice"]) # multilingual billing # multilingual technical ``` > **Long documents on the checkpoints: `laya-multilingual` reads up to 8,192 tokens.** It ships with a 1,024-token limit that cuts long documents off, so pass `max_len=8192` for them: > > ```python > result = router.predict(long_document, questions, model="multilingual", max_len=8192) > ``` > > In the table above, 16 to 18 of 20 requests were answered correctly with up to about 4,000 tokens of text before them; beyond that results vary (8 to 17 of 20), so check long-document accuracy on your own data. Short inputs give identical answers with `max_len=8192`, and speed follows the input's real length, not the limit: short inputs are unchanged, and a 4,000-token input takes about 1.7 s on an Apple GPU. Name the checkpoint with `model="multilingual"`, since long mostly-English text would otherwise route to the English checkpoint. With `vegaml=True` none of this applies: the reader takes 73,728 tokens whole. From the command line, `laya "My payment failed twice" --preset triage` answers a ready-made question set. More in the [full quickstart](#quickstart-route-mode-recommended) and the [docs](https://nandhakishorm.github.io/laya/). ## Fine-tune for better accuracy The shipped checkpoints work zero-shot, but fine-tuning on decisions from your own domain is where accuracy jumps. On the typed-decisions benchmark (2,000 decisions across four workflows), the fine-tuned `laya-typed-decisions` checkpoint scores **0.766** accuracy, against **0.362** for the base English checkpoint on the same decisions. **[Fine-tuning notebook](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/notebooks/laya_finetune_typed_decisions_2xT4_kaggle.ipynb)** (Kaggle 2xT4) and **[Apple Silicon script](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/notebooks/laya_finetune_typed_decisions_mps.py)** (MPS / CPU): run the whole loop (build dataset, train with RLCD, calibrate temperatures, evaluate, export).
